draft.title: Islamic bioethics
card: Bioethics asks what is right in medicine and the start and end of life. Muslims answer by drawing on the belief that life is a trust from God, and that God gives life and sets its span.
Sharia is Islamic law and guidance. It draws on the Quran and Hadith, and scholars use it to judge new medical questions.
Most Muslim scholars reject it, because ending a life on purpose takes a decision that belongs to God. Caring for a patient and easing pain is still encouraged.
Many scholars accept IVF when it uses the sperm and egg of a married couple, as it helps them have children within marriage. Views differ on matters such as donor gametes.
draft.remember: Islamic bioethics starts from life belonging to God and applies sharia to each case.

a.q: Why do most Muslim scholars reject euthanasia?
opts: Life belongs to God, so ending it is not a human choice
Sharia forbids doctors from treating dying patients
Islam teaches that pain should never be eased
Sharia has no guidance on questions about medicine
a.why: Most scholars hold that God gives life and sets its span, so deliberately ending a life takes a decision that is God's. The idea that care is forbidden is wrong, because easing pain and caring for patients is still encouraged.
a.clue: Think about who decides when life ends.

b.q: Amira and Omar are a married couple in Lakemba who cannot conceive. Their imam says IVF using their own sperm and egg is generally acceptable. Which reasoning best explains his view?
opts: It helps a married couple have children within marriage
Medicine may override God's will whenever a couple wishes
Islam sees no link between human life and God's will
Sharia allows any IVF method, including donor gametes
b.why: The imam's view rests on sharia, which scholars apply to the case: the treatment helps a married couple have children within marriage. The option that all methods are allowed is wrong, because the card says views differ on matters such as donor gametes.
b.clue: Note that the couple is married and uses only their own gametes.

a.best: Life belongs to God, so ending it is not a human choice

b.best: It helps a married couple have children within marriage

proposal.title: Islamic bioethics
card: Bioethics asks what is right in medicine and at the start and end of life. Muslims draw on the belief that life is a trust from God, and that God gives life and sets its span.
Sharia is Islamic law and guidance, drawn from the Quran and Hadith. These texts do not name euthanasia or IVF, so scholars reason from their principles to judge such cases.
Most Muslim scholars reject it, because ending a life on purpose takes a decision that belongs to God. Caring for a patient and easing pain is still encouraged.
Many scholars accept IVF when it uses the sperm and egg of a husband and wife, as it helps them have children within marriage. Views differ on matters such as donor sperm or eggs.
proposal.remember: Islamic bioethics starts from life belonging to God and applies sharia to each case.

a.q: Why do most Muslim scholars reject euthanasia?
opts: Life is a trust from God, who sets its span
Suffering is a test, so pain relief should be refused
The Quran mentions euthanasia by name and bans it
Only a doctor, not the patient, may decide to end life
a.why: Most scholars hold that God gives life and sets its span, so deliberately ending a life is not a human decision, whether by patient or doctor. The Quran does not name euthanasia: scholars reach their view by reasoning from its principles, and easing pain is still encouraged.
a.clue: Think about who decides when a life ends.

b.q: Amira and Omar, a husband and wife in Lakemba, cannot conceive. Their imam says IVF with Omar's sperm and Amira's egg can be acceptable. What reasoning best supports his view?
opts: It helps them have a child within their marriage
Sharia leaves fertility choices to each couple alone
Any IVF method is allowed if both partners consent
IVF is named and approved in the Quran
b.why: Scholars who accept IVF do so because, with the husband's sperm and the wife's egg, it helps a couple have children within marriage. Consent alone is not enough, since views differ on donor sperm or eggs. The Quran does not name IVF, and scholars, not each couple alone, apply sharia to the case.
b.clue: Think about whose sperm and egg are used, and why that matters.
